articles.excerpt: I run a visa agency in Bali. The other half of my week goes into Apify Actors, and one of them scrapes a page type that only exists because a law says it must: the Impressum. Every business website in…
articles.body: I run a visa agency in Bali. The other half of my week goes into Apify Actors, and one of them scrapes a page type that only exists because a law says it must: the Impressum . Every business website in Germany, Austria and Switzerland has to publish one, and it has to carry things no marketing page ever would — the legal company name, the people who run it (Geschäftsführer, Inhaber, Vorstand), the register court and HRB / FN / UID number, the VAT ID, a real postal address and a real email. For B2B lead work that is unusually good data. A Google Maps export gives you info@ and a phone number. An Impressum gives you the name of the person who signs things , plus a register number you can verify. One domain in, one row out. That is the theory.

In 2026, three platforms make this dramatically easier: Hugging Face (the model hub turned cloud), Replicate (the developer-friendly inference platform), and Together AI (the performance-focused API provider). articles.body: At the end of October, Google opened a plugin catalog for Antigravity, its new platform for agentic development. We built a Publora plugin, submitted it and are now waiting to hear back. I don't write the code myself. Claude does that, while I ask questions, test things and deal with the submissions. I've become fairly familiar with the last part over the past year. Chrome rejected our extension twice. Canva took forty-seven days and five versions. Zapier sent us through eight rounds. By now, when I hear "plugin marketplace," I expect documentation, several forms, a reviewer and at least one email explaining what we've done wrong. Antigravity asked us to fill out a Google Form.

articles.title: Why every standard bet on a single-zero roulette wheel has the same expected value
articles.excerpt: A single-zero roulette wheel offers about ten standard bets: a single number, two numbers, a row of three, a block of four, red or black, a dozen, and so on. They pay very different amounts, from 35 t…
articles.body: A single-zero roulette wheel offers about ten standard bets: a single number, two numbers, a row of three, a block of four, red or black, a dozen, and so on. They pay very different amounts, from 35 to 1 down to 1 to 1. Yet every one of them has exactly the same expected value: −1/37 of the stake . That follows from one line of arithmetic. It's also a clean example of expected value, exact fractions, and how little the mean tells you about a random variable. The code blocks below form one script: paste them into a single .mjs file in order and node prints the output shown under each. The setup A European wheel has 37 pockets: the numbers 1 to 36 plus a single 0. Each spin lands on one pocket uniformly at random. A bet covers c pockets and pays p to 1 .

articles.title: Symfony performance tips
articles.excerpt: Building large services with many dependencies brings a whole range of performance problems. Initializing and loading such a service costs us memory, CPU, and request processing time. Let's look at th…
articles.body: Building large services with many dependencies brings a whole range of performance problems. Initializing and loading such a service costs us memory, CPU, and request processing time. Let's look at three basic techniques for optimizing services in Symfony while keeping the code clean. 1. Divide and conquer Symfony can inject a service directly into a controller method argument. Don't build a "god service". Split operations into separate micro-services, each with a single responsibility. Every service then calls only what it really needs. As a bonus you get a better structure, cleaner code, and easier refactoring down the road.

There was just one problem: it was English-only. For a tool designed to help global businesses and designers, this was a major barrier. Today, we rolled out a major update. The entire Brand Color Extractor is now natively translated into 10 languages, complete with full Right-to-Left (RTL) layout support. Here is a look at how we handled the localization entirely on the client side. The Translation Architecture Since RahaLune is a 100% client-side app, we didn't want to rely on an external API to fetch translations. We needed the site to remain fast, even if a user switches languages multiple times.

Reflect Orbital has made significant progress to date. articles.body: One of the key innovations in GTA 5 is about to be replicated in GTA 6 — character switching. We've already seen this in the trailers, as the player switched control between driver and gunner while evading police. While GTA 6 features dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, you can freely switch between, GTA 5 had three of them: Franklin, Trevor, and Michael. Out in the open world, you could switch and the camera would shoot into the sky for a satellite view of the city before zooming back down to the character you’d chosen. A certain kind of doomsayer has presented GTA 6 as, metaphorically, the Last Video Game, an extinction-level event, a monumentally excessive fiddle solo performed by Nero amid a burning Rome. articles.title: Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns
articles.excerpt: More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.
articles.body: More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye. That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that currently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town. The results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak.
